text:
One would think the town,
after crossing the valley,
lost its reason
and drew itself a single street.


And so beneath the mountain range
it stationed itself feverishly like spring.


In its windows alcohol
is mixed with sun.


Its women and its flowers
speak the dialect of colors.


And the little stream that runs like a horse
drags the hens along in February and May.


Down the sidewalk pass
the priest, the cow, and the last light alike.


Here nothing of greater consequence than roses
ever happens.


As if rain threatened,
the afternoon that was blond has turned brown.


It seems the breeze
is trying out a perfume and a new turn.


A song unfolds a smile for me
and sinks a sigh into me.

translation.title: One Would Think the Town...
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish rendering. The town's personification, color dialect, animal movement, and lightly comic final image are preserved.
